clue.text: Without consideration from a worker

parts.note: off can mean away from, as in taking a book off the shelf
a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a labourer acted thoughtlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is easy to skip as a link word, but here it supplies OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand remark is casual and thoughtless, made with no care or forethought.

clue.text: On television watch the scene

definitions.meaning: to watch a programme on television is to see it as a viewer
a scene before one's eyes, such as a vista from a window

explanation.surface: Someone tunes in to watch what is happening on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: To view is to look at something, such as a broadcast; a view is also the vista or prospect seen.

clue.text: Ready to be won over. having a meal Ben prepared

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Ben cooks a meal, perhaps to soften someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the letters of A MEAL plus BEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is open to persuasion and willing to agree.

clue.text: Rely completely in an unsuspecting way

parts.note: to rely on someone is to trust them
fully means completely or wholly

explanation.surface: Advice to depend wholly on someone, without suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without suspicion means acting with naive faith in others, believing them readily.

clue.text: Reservoir pupils used to dip into

definitions.text: Reservoir pupils used to dip into

parts.words: Reservoir pupils used to dip into
parts.note: a schoolroom memory: the small pot sunk into an old school desk, into which children dipped their pens

explanation.surface: A water supply where schoolchildren once went swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservoir' suggests a lake for swimming, but it is the little container of writing fluid set into old school desks.
explanation.definitionFit: Old classroom desks held a small pot of writing fluid into which pupils dipped their dip pens.

clue.text: Unusually fair may be one from the Dark Continent

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters of the word fair are put in an odd order

parts.note: may and can both express permission or possibility

explanation.surface: A remark that an unusually fair-skinned person might still come from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges FAIR into AFRI. 'The Dark Continent' is an old, now dated name for Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone native to Africa, the continent once called dark by European explorers, is described by that adjective.

clue.text: Before midday if not in love with Cupid

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the hours before noon
or introduces an alternative, meaning if not
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic in the morning, not yet in love, meeting the god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: An amorino is a small chubby winged figure of the love god, common in Italian art.

clue.text: Lady angler, one going in search of gems

definitions.text: one going in search of gems

parts.note: Pearl is a woman's first name
a fisher is one who fishes, an angler

explanation.surface: A woman who likes fishing turns out to be a treasure hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady' is a girl's name here, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver who seeks oysters for their precious lustrous beads does this job.

clue.text: Noticed name that had been cut

parts.note: to have noticed something is to have seen it

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a name that had been deleted from a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber that has been cut with a toothed blade is described by this past participle.

clue.text: Sneak in lat

parts.note: taken as written
late can mean former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Someone slips in after hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like a time of arrival, but it means one-time or former.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is a telltale who reports on others, the same as a grass or snitch.

clue.text: Love faint smell of varying hues

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
faint and pale both mean weak or washed out in colour
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: A lover catches a faint, shifting perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a milky shimmer that changes colour like a gemstone is described this way.

clue.text: Happened to be next to the mountain

indicators.note: next to places one piece beside the other in the answer

parts.note: taken as the plain verb be
a fell is a hill or mountain in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone happened to find themselves beside a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: FELL is a word for a hill in the Lake District and other northern English uplands.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell is an old-fashioned verb meaning took place or occurred.

clue.text: Dispose of one fancy clue, make fun of it

parts.note: to rid oneself of something is to dispose of it
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters of the word clue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver throws out a fanciful clue and mocks it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or deride someone is to laugh at them scornfully.

clue.text: Height right of figure outside

indicators.note: the figure goes outside the letter for right, so it encloses that letter

parts.note: a statue is a sculpted figure

explanation.surface: A measurement of how tall a statue is, taken from its right side.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's natural standing height or build.

clue.text: Short preliminary passage, it is an anthem

parts.note: intro is a short form of introduction, an opening passage of music
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician describes the opening of a choral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' is part of the first piece: the shortened word for introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is a psalm or antiphon sung as the priest approaches the altar at the start of Mass.

clue.text: Await a sober conclusion

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who does not drink alcohol
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Someone waits for a party to end soberly.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage to attend upon something is to wait for it or be ready for it.

clue.text: Wandering from Tring, say

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the answer is built by rearranging the letters of the following words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has strayed far from Tring, a small market town in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the letters of TRING SAY being reworked. Tring is a small town in Hertfordshire, north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To be wandering is to be roaming off the right path, drifting away.

clue.text: Nasal hair Len heartlessly removed

indicators.note: removed means moved out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the name is taken away

explanation.surface: Len has had his nose hair plucked out without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes E from LEN to leave LN; 'removed' then rearranges HAIR plus LN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinal is a technical adjective for things relating to the nose.

clue.text: Duck having twitch of the ear

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like the letter O
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A duck with a twitching ear.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is a medical adjective meaning relating to the ear.

clue.text: Believe eccentric has a means with which to pay

definitions.text: a means with which to pay

parts.note: to credit a story is to believe it
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: An odd character believes he can pay for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic payment card lets the holder buy now on borrowed money.

clue.text: Smack on the wrist

definitions.meaning: a blow with the open hand, as in a clip round the ear
the end part of a sleeve that goes round the wrist

explanation.surface: A slap on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuff means both a light blow with the hand and the band at the end of a sleeve.

clue.text: Crease that needs to be ironed out

definitions.meaning: a fold or line in fabric or skin

definitions.text: that needs to be ironed out
definitions.meaning: a minor problem or flaw to be smoothed away before something works

explanation.surface: A crumpled shirt waiting for the iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkle is both a crumple in cloth and a small snag in a plan.

clue.text: Fool with a fraction of intelligence?

parts.note: a half is a fraction
wit means intelligence or good sense

explanation.surface: A dimwit has only part of the brains he needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay pictures a person with only part of a brain, which is the meaning too.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a stupid person, a dunce.
